title: Grateful Dead Live at Academy of Music on 1972-03-23
lineage: Dat (Sony D8) -> Samplitude Professional v9.11 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Apogee AD500 -> Dat (48k)

ai_review.summary: A pristine soundboard capture of the March 23 1972 Academy show delivers crystal‑clear audio and a high‑energy set highlighted by a soaring Dark Star and the historic pedal‑steel Looks Like Rain.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑restored soundboard is virtually flawless—crisp, balanced, and free of major drop‑outs—making every nuance audible. Musically the performance is electric, with a monster Dark Star, an unforgettable first‑time pedal‑steel “Looks Like Rain,” and standout renditions of Cumberland, Two Souls In Communion and the Not Fade Away sandwich. Overall the show radiates high energy and tight playing throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 detailed reviews overwhelmingly praise both the performance (many 5‑star comments on Dark Star, LLR, overall energy) and the recording (soundboard noted as crisp/excellent). Minor criticisms are sparse and do not detract from the overall excellence.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with superb balance; occasional tiny buzzes/pops noted but considered part of the live power. Reviewers repeatedly call it “fantastic,” “beautiful sonic delight,” and “flawless.”

standout_songs: Not Fade Away > Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad
show_quality.setlist_flow: A marathon first set (~18 songs, 2 hrs) that stays concise and tight, followed by an expansive second set packed with jams (Dark Star, Playing in the Band) and classic sandwich finishes; pacing keeps momentum high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his melodic guitar tone, pedal‑steel work on Looks Like Rain, and “tight” lead vocals; described as fast, flexible, and a highlight of the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for powerful bass lines in Dark Star (“awesome stuff”) and prominent backing vocals on Looks Like Rain; several reviewers call his singing “glorious.”
band_member_comments.Bob: Complimented for strong rhythm guitar, vigorous lead vocals (e.g., Big Boss Man), and overall “pumped up” presence.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s organ work highlighted as a driving force in the early‑’72 sound; Pigpen’s contributions are mentioned as “wild” and essential to the show’s blues/rock blend.
